transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
My moods have been all over the place lately, and I feel wound up and irritated with everyone at home. It just feels like I can't calm down, and I've been snapping at the people I love most.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or “up,” needed much less sleep, and still felt fine the next day? If so, did those periods last several days or more?

Yes, I've been waking up after only a few hours of sleep buzzing with energy, and I'll immediately start cleaning or cooking at 3 a.m. because I just can't sit still. This has been going on consistently for about a month now, and during this time, I often feel on top of the world but also highly wound up.

Before this current month-long period, have you ever had a separate episode of depression lasting at least 2 weeks where you felt very down or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day? Or have you had any similar “up” periods in the past?

No, I haven't really had periods like this before, or at least nothing nearly this severe. I also don't recall ever having a two-week period of deep depression where I felt down or lost interest in things. This current month is really what stands out as being completely different for me.

During this past month, have you had any experiences like hearing voices, feeling especially suspicious, or believing things others said weren’t true? Has this caused serious problems at work, school, finances, or relationships, or led to hospitalization?

No, I haven't experienced anything like hearing voices or paranoia, and I haven't been hospitalized. But it has caused huge problems—I'm making mistakes at my warehouse job, spending money we don't have, and constantly arguing with my family. It got so bad that my husband and pastor insisted I come to the clinic because they're worried I'm spinning out of control.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first episode of persistently elevated/irritable mood with increased energy lasting about one month, marked decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and significant impairment in work, finances, and relationships, without psychotic symptoms. There is no history of prior major depressive episodes or prior similar episodes. This is most consistent with mania without psychotic symptoms.
